Lemma
[Time derivative of a parametrix convolution] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0270, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0271 ↗ lem:chow-iii-ch23-parametrix-integration-continuity 1. ch23:23.29\group Convolution differentiation

For continuous $G$, \[ \partial _t(P_N*G)(x,y,t)=G(x,y,t)+\int _0^t\int _{\mathcal M} \partial _tP_N(x,z,t-s)G(z,y,s)\, d\mu (z)\, ds. \]
Proof

\sketch Write the convolution as $\int _0^tJ_N(s,t)\, ds$. The upper endpoint tends to $G(x,y,t)$ by the approximate-identity lemma, while the difference quotient of $J_N$ converges under the integral by the same Gaussian domination.

□
